title: Decide relay signer identity binding: truncated signer-ID field vs SIID-indexed TOFU lookup vs signed-payload two-hop chains
description:
DECISION NEEDED: relay signer identity binding for link frames (decomposed from project-LICHEN-2auf.44.9.8). The wire-format choice is Mark's.

== CURRENT STATE (evidence, as of 2026-08-28 tree) ==
The premise "link frame omits a signer identifier" is STALE: the closed Schnorr-48 wire migration (project-LICHEN-2auf.35) added a mandatory 8-byte Signer Identifier (SIID) to every signed frame.
- spec/02-physical-link.md 4.1-4.2: SIID (0/8B) after Dst Addr; LLSec SI bit 7; signed frames MUST set S+SI; transcript "LICHEN-LINK-v1"||0x00||LENGTH||LLSec||Epoch||SeqNum||DST_LEN||DstAddr||SIID||Payload binds the exact 8 SIID octets; "the selected trust-store public key, rather than SIID by itself, establishes the authenticated sender identity".
- Re-sign call sites: rust/lichen-link/src/relay.rs:83 relay_verified_frame (verify inbound against pinned upstream key, then re-sign with own key/own SIID/own counter); C lichen/subsys/lichen/link/lichen_link_tx.c:235 lichen_link_relay_raw and :348 lichen_link_relay_frame (same pattern).
- Key resolution today: Rust indexed lookup peers.get(&signer_iid) (link_layer.rs:1117); Python pinned-key cache keyed by canonical IID (link_layer.py); C uses O(N) constant-time trial-verify over the provisioned peer table (l2/lichen_l2_peer.c:118 peer_try_all_pubkeys) with TOFU pinning (lichen_l2_peer.c:306) and post-match SIID<->canonical-EUI64 binding (lichen_link_rx.c:196-203). No implementation derives the key from the preserved IPv6 source.
- Vectors: test/vectors/wire_format_v2.json already covers SI+S normal / relay-resigned / malformed frames and hop re-signing inputs.
RESIDUAL GAP: spec leaves key-SELECTION policy open (SIID is "routing hint only until the signature verifies"); C's selection is correct and fail-closed but is whole-table trial verification (CPU cost on STM32WL-class: up to CONFIG_LICHEN_LINK_MAX_NEIGHBORS Schnorr-48 verifies per frame) rather than SIID-indexed lookup, and relay-neighbor TOFU cache semantics (populate/evict) are not normative.

== BYTE BUDGET (spec/02 4.1; rust frame.rs MAX_FRAME_LEN=255, MAX_FRAME_BODY=254) ==
Signed-frame fixed overhead: LLSec(1)+Epoch(1)+SeqNum(2)+SIID(8)+Sig(48) = 60B, plus DstAddr(0/2/8). Payload budget = 254-60-dst_len = 194B broadcast / 192B short / 186B extended. Length field: 1B, body 4-254B, LoRa total cap 255B.
(a) 0B if SIID stays 8B (status quo); shrinking SIID to 4B truncation saves 4B (payload 190/198) but is a breaking transcript change (SI flag implies exactly 8 on-wire octets today).
(b) 0B wire change.
(c) +8B if signer identity duplicated inside payload (or 0B reusing transcript SIID); adds a second signature verify per hop.

== OPTIONS ==
(a) Explicit truncated signer ID in frame (4-8B of relay IID/key hash).
  Wire cost: 4B saved only if SIID shrinks 8->4B; no saving if added alongside.
  Security: SIID remains an untrusted hint (signature still binds the trust-store key), but 32-bit truncation invites SIID-space collisions -> wrong-candidate lookups -> verify fails (DoS/confusion, not forgery). 8B form is strictly stronger and already shipped.
  Cross-impl churn: HIGH. Transcript definition change; C/Rust/Python parsers+signers; flag-day upgrade semantics per spec 4.1 ("MUST NOT accept both transcripts for the same frame").
  Vector impact: full regeneration of link_frame.json, link_frame_signed_modes.json, wire_format_v2.json, link-edge-fuzz.json, frame_length_boundaries.json.
(b) Deterministic lookup: verifier resolves the key from the TOFU key cache keyed by the frame's link-layer signer address (SIID -> canonical EUI-64 -> pinned key); no wire change.
  Wire cost: 0B. wire_format_v2 stays valid.
  Security: claimant without the pinned key fails transcript verify (key substitution rejected); SIID never allocates state pre-verify (spec 4.2 already mandates); replay stays keyed by (pubkey, key-generation). Relay spoofing fails closed. Cache semantics must be normative: pin on first VERIFIED contact, reject key mismatch for a pinned SIID (TOFU violation), eviction only per trust-store policy.
  Cross-impl churn: LOW-MEDIUM. Rust/Python already indexed; C replaces/augments peer_try_all_pubkeys with SIID-indexed lookup (keep constant-time properties or document trade), adds relay TOFU population. Spec gains one normative paragraph.
  Vector impact: none for wire bytes; add cross-impl cache-behavior and 3-node A->B->C relay-chain vectors (C's cache pins B, not A).
(c) Signer identity inside signed payload + two-hop verification chains.
  Wire cost: ~0-8B; verifier must validate relay sig AND origin sig.
  Security: adds end-to-end origin attribution at link layer, but origin cannot predict per-hop mutations (Hop Limit, RFC 6554 SRH address swaps), so origin-sig scope is ill-defined; doubles Schnorr-48 verifies per hop (constrained MCU cost); doubles replay state; duplicates the existing DAO Origin Signature profile (lichen/subsys/lichen/link/sos_origin.c, application-layer, domain-separated per draft-lichen-schnorr-00 8).
  Cross-impl churn: VERY HIGH (spec 8.4 hop-by-hop model rewrite + all impls).
  Vector impact: full regeneration + new chain vectors.

== RECOMMENDATION ==
Option (b). The wire already carries the strongest form of (a) - a full 8-byte transcript-bound SIID - so truncation buys 4B at breaking-transcript cost, and (c) duplicates the SOS/DAO origin signature with 2x verify cost and ill-defined scope across SRH mutations. The open problem is key-selection policy: make SIID-indexed TOFU trust-store lookup normative in spec 02 (4.1/4.2) and align C to Rust/Python behavior. Child implementation beads are filed, gated on this decision.
acceptance_criteria: Mark selects one option (a/b/c); selection recorded on this bead; child beads unblocked or superseded accordingly.
